questions.question: Who was the founder of a non-violent movement named as "Khudai Khidmatgars"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Khudai Khidmatgars was a non-violent movement in the North-West Frontier Province of British India, which is now in Pakistan.**
 
• The movement was started by** Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan,** who was also known as the **Frontier Gandhi.**
 
• The Khudai Khidmatgars were also known as the **"Red Shirts**" because of the **color** of their uniforms.
 
• **The movement was based on the principles of non-violence, social justice, and democracy.**
 
• The Khudai Khidmatgars played an important role in the** Indian independence movement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **C. Rajagopalachari was a prominent Indian politician and independence activist.**

 
 
• He was the **last Governor-General **of India.
 
 
 
• **Mohammad Ali Jinnah was the founder of Pakistan and the leader of the All India Muslim League.**
 
 
• He played a major role** **in the partition of India.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi was the leader of the Indian independence movement and is known for his principles of non-violence.**
 
 
• He was a close associate of Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan and supported the** Khudai Khidmatgars.**

questions.question: Which of the following metal is always a component in an amalgam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mercury.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mercury is always a component in an amalgam because it is a liquid metal at room temperature and easily mixes with other metals to form a solid alloy.**
 
• Amalgam is a** dental filling **material that has been used for over 150 years and is made by mixing mercury with other metals such as **silver, tin, and copper.**
 
• Strontium is not** **commonly used in dental materials and is not a component of amalgam.
 
• Zinc is used in** some dental materials** but is not always a component of amalgam.
 
• **Aluminum is not used in dental amalgam due to its potential toxicity and reactivity with mercury.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Strontium is a chemical element with atomic number 38.**

 
 
• It is a **soft, silvery-white metal** that is used in some alloys and as a **radioactive tracer** in medical imaging.
 
 
 
• **Zinc is a chemical element with atomic number 30.**
 
 
• **​**It is a **bluish-white meta**l that is used in a variety of applications, including as a component in **dental materials** and as a** **dietary supplement.
 
 
 
• **Aluminum is a chemical element with atomic number 13.**
 
 
• **​**It is a lightweight**, **silvery-white** **metal that is used in a wide range of applications, including in **construction, packaging, and transportation. **

questions.question: Bhimbetka caves are situated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Bhimbetka caves are located in** **Madhya Pradesh, India.**
 
• These caves are known for their prehistoric rock paintings and have been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• **The paintings in the caves depict the life of early humans, their daily activities, and their relationship with animals.**
 
• These caves were discovered by V.S. Wakankar in 1957and have since then been a major tourist attraction.
 
• **Rajasthan, Haryana, and Gujarat **are also home to several ancient caves and rock paintings, but Bhimbetka caves are specifically located in Madhya Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​**Haryana is home to the Surajkund lake, which is surrounded by several ancient temples and caves, including the famous Bhuteshwar temple and Karna lake caves.**
 
• Gujarat is home to the famous Junagadh caves, which are known for their intricate rock-cut architecture and sculptures.
 
• **​These caves were built during the reign of Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.**

questions.question: Treasury bills are issued by the _______.

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Treasury bills are short-term securities issued by the Government of India. **
 
• Treasury bills are issued by the government to raise short-term funds to meet its expenditure needs.
 
• **The bills are issued at a discount to their face value, and the difference between the face value and the issue price is the interest earned by the investor.**
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India acts as the issuing and paying agent for the government in the issuance of treasury bills.**
 
• The bills are issued for a tenure of** 91 days, 182 days, and 364 days**, and are highly liquid as they can be easily traded in the secondary market

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) **is the regulatory body that oversees the functioning of the** **securities market in India and regulates the activities of various market intermediaries such as** stockbrokers, mutual funds, and portfolio managers.**
 
• **Insurance Regulatory Authority of India (IRDA) is the regulatory body that oversees the functioning of the insurance industry in India and regulates the activities of insurance companies, agents, and brokers.**

questions.question: In the Indian subcontinent, how many country/countries share its land frontiers with every member country of the subcontinent?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** One.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
**India** is the central country in the subcontinent and shares land borders with Pakistan, Nepal, Bhutan, China, Bangladesh, and Myanmar.

 
 
• 
 
Bangladesh shares land borders with India and Myanmar (with Myanmar not being a core country of the Indian subcontinent traditionally).

 
 
• 
 
Nepal and Bhutan share borders only with India.

 Pakistan shares a land border with India and Afghanistan (with Afghanistan sometimes being considered part of the subcontinent).

 
 
• 
 
Given this setup, India is the only country that shares its land borders with all other traditionally recognized member countries of the Indian subcontinent (Pakistan, Nepal, Bhutan, China and Bangladesh).

 
 
• 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is : One

 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian subcontinent is a region in** South Asia** that includes** India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives. **
 
• India is the **largest country** in the Indian subcontinent and shares its borders with **Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, and Myanmar.**
 
• **Pakistan shares its borders with India, Afghanistan, Iran, and China.**
 
• **Nepal** shares its borders with **India and China.**
 
• **Bhutan** shares its borders with **India and China.**
 
• **Sri Lanka and the Maldives are island countries and do not share their borders with any other member country of the Indian subcontinent.**

questions.question: How many Fundamental Duties were added in the Constitution of India by the 42nd Amendment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental duties were added to the Constitution of India through the 42nd Amendment in 1976.**
 
• The amendment added a total of **10 Fundamental Duties** under** Article 51A **of the Constitution.
 
• These duties are **non-justiciable,** which means that they cannot be enforced by law.
 
• The aim of adding Fundamental Duties was to promote a sense of **responsibility and patriotism** among citizens towards the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Russian Constitution** served as the model for the concept of Fundamental Duties.
 
• **In addition to the original 10 duties, one more was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002.**
 
• According to the **Ranganath Mishra** ruling from the Supreme Court in** 2003,** social sanctions** **should also be used to enforce fundamental duties.
 
• **The Supreme Court ruled in AIIMS Students Union v. AIIMS 2001 that fundamental duties are just as significant as fundamental rights.​**

questions.question: The number of live births per thousand persons in a year is called _________.
questions.solution:

• There are two main types of cells:** prokaryotic cells,** which are simple cells without a nucleus, and** eukaryotic cells,** which are more complex cells with a nucleus and organelles.

• Health issues can result from having too much or too little of a specific enzyme.
 
• Healthcare professionals can also use the enzymes in our blood to check for** **injuries and illnesses.
 
 
 
• **Hormones are signaling molecules that regulate various physiological processes.**
 
 
• **Numerous bodily processes, including growth, repair, and reproduction, are regulated by hormones.**
 
• Numerous organ systems and hormones are part of the **endocrine system.**​

questions.question: The satellites orbit the earth in which of the following layers of the atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Exosphere.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Satellites orbit the earth in the exosphere, which is the outermost layer of the atmosphere.**
 
• The exosphere starts at an altitude of about** 500 km **above the earth's surface and extends to about **10,000 km.**
 
• **This layer is characterized by extremely low density and high temperatures due to the intense solar radiation.**
 
• Satellites that orbit in the exosphere include **communication, navigation, and weather satellites.**

• The **exosphere **is the **outermost layer **of the atmosphere, where satellites orbit the earth.
 
• The stratosphere is the layer above the troposphere, and it contains the ozone layer. 
 
• The mesosphere is the layer above the stratosphere and below the thermosphere. 
 
• **The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, where we live and where weather occurs.**
